memoryText: And let them make me a sanctuary, that I may dwell in their midst.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Exodus 25:8 slowly, several times, and then say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
Exodus 25:8 is the heart of the tabernacle instructions. It is easy to lose it among the details of cubits and curtains, so give it a day to rest in your mind.

“Let them make me a sanctuary.” The word “sanctuary” means a holy place, a place set apart. God is not asking for an ordinary building. He is asking for a place where the holy can meet the human.

“That I may dwell.” This is the purpose clause. The God who made heaven and earth wants to live among his creatures. The verb is the root of the word “tabernacle” and of the Hebrew term shekinah, which later Jewish writers used for the presence of God. The whole Bible will keep returning to this theme: God wants to be with us.

“In their midst.” The tabernacle was placed at the very center of the camp, with the tribes arranged around it on every side. God did not set himself apart on the edge. He lived in the middle of his people.

For the Christian, the verse points forward to Jesus, who “dwelt among us” (John 1:14), and to the church, which is “a holy temple in the Lord” and “a dwelling place for God by the Spirit” (Ephesians 2:21-22). It points forward as well to the day when “the dwelling place of God is with man” forever (Revelation 21:3).
weekInReview: This week you left the covenant at Sinai and began to read the instructions for the tabernacle. You saw the ark and the mercy seat, the table, the lampstand, and the curtains and veil of the tent. You saw the bronze altar and the courtyard, and you read about the garments of the priests, including the breastpiece with the names of the twelve tribes. The pattern is clear: God wants to dwell among his people, and he provides both a place and a mediator to make it possible. The week taught that approach to God is always by way of a sacrifice and a priest.
reflectionQuestions: The tabernacle had a gate, an altar, a veil, and a priest between God and the people. What does this teach you about the way to approach a holy God?
How is Jesus the true tabernacle and the true high priest? What difference does it make that the veil is torn and you can come near through him?
Where in your daily life do you most need to remember that God is near and wants to be with you? Write a short prayer asking him to make his presence real to you.
prayerPrompts: Thank God for making his home with his people.
Ask him to help you carry that nearness into the week.
